searchText: <@!301186049323958275> I don't know where you want to talk about the lack of global semaphore, but this is where mev-geth comes from. Wherever is fine, here if you like or elsewhere if there is a better place. 🙂 Yeah, I just don't see how we can have functional gossip when there is MEV, and we have MEV because two transactions in the same block can modify the same state. Ah, you want each state entry to be touchable by one transaction per block? e.g., one Uniswap trade between a particular pair per block Well, I don't want that, but that fixes the problem 😄 It is an interesting point. My gut tells me that would have some pretty severe side effects, but maybe it can be the root of some better design. Perhaps contracts could opt-in to it? Flag certain state entries as "once per block"? Another way to fix the problem is to add conditionals to transactions that say, only execute my transaction against this list of merkle leafs. Another way is to assert the transaction will only pay the miner if the merkle leafs have a particular value at the end of the block. in some semi-stateless world these sorts of transactions are maybe literally 100x more reasonable than the current model, where DoSing would be trivial. we have to really constrain the search that tx can trigger on the miner side. the easiest way to do that is to make the user provide the result of the search with the transaction. I like these ideas. They are new to me and I need to think on them more though.
